title: Space Bound for a Bounded Loop Search
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words. Let $g$ be a state-update function, $A$ an acceptance test, $o$ an output function, $s_0$ an initial-state function, and $R,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Assume that $F$ computes the function sending an input $x$ to the binary expansion of $R(|x|)$ within time $T(|x|)$; that $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds and is preserved by $g$; and that, from the initial configuration of $B$ on $x$, some time $t\le T(|x|)$ reaches the seam configuration with state $a$ and tape contents given by $s_0(x)$, with no earlier time having state $a$. Assume also that for every $x,s$ with $I(x,s)$, there is a time $t$ with $0<t\le T(|x|)$ such that no time strictly between $0$ and $t$ has state $a$ when started from the seam configuration for $(x,s)$; at time $t$, if $A(x,s)$ holds, the machine halts with output $o(x,s)$, and otherwise it reaches the seam configuration for $(x,g(x,s))$. Then there is a finite Turing machine $E$ and a natural number $c$ such that, on every input $x$, $E$ computes the result of searching the iterates $g^i(x,s_0(x))$ for the least $i\le R(|x|)$ satisfying $A(x,g^i(x,s_0(x)))$, returning $o(x,g^i(x,s_0(x)))$ if one is found and the empty word otherwise, within time $c(T(|x|)+1)(R(|x|)+2)$. Moreover, for every input $x$ and every time $t$, the space used by $E$ by time $t$ is at most $c(T(|x|)+1)$.
